headline: Bedrocan collapse strains medical cannabis supply in Italy and the UK
dek: The Dutch grower's bankruptcy cuts off the main source for Italian pharmacies and a UK epilepsy oil, as a bidder negotiates for its remaining stock.
key_points: A Dutch court declared Bedrocan International and Bedrocan Nederland bankrupt on 8 October, after the state cannabis office ended its supply contract on 1 January.
Italy received 1,695 kg of medical cannabis in 2024, of which only a little over 200 kg was grown at home, leaving it heavily dependent on the Dutch channel.
About seven UK prescriptions for Bedrolite, mostly children with severe epilepsy, are affected; the UK maker says it has roughly six months of stock.
A party is negotiating with the bankruptcy trustee to take over Bedrocan's medicinal cannabis stock, regional paper DVHN reported on 4 November.
body: The bankruptcy of Bedrocan, the Dutch grower that for more than two decades supplied the Netherlands' state medical cannabis programme, is turning into a supply problem far beyond Dutch borders. Italy, which imports most of its medical cannabis through the Dutch channel, and a small group of UK children with severe epilepsy are the most exposed.

A Dutch court declared Bedrocan International B.V. and Bedrocan Nederland B.V. bankrupt on 8 October, ending a brief suspension of payments. On 4 November, regional paper DVHN reported, via the national insolvency register, that a party is negotiating with the trustee to take over the company's stock of medicinal cannabis, and that a restart of the business is not yet certain.

The trigger was a gap in Dutch policy. The Office of Medicinal Cannabis, part of the health ministry, had bought most of Bedrocan's output since 2003 and distributed it to Dutch pharmacies and abroad. That contract ended on 1 January 2026. The government is reforming the system so private growers can sell directly to pharmacies and foreign buyers, but Health Minister Sophie Hermans has said the change will not take effect before July 2028, Il Post reported. Until the Opium Act is amended, Bedrocan could not sell to pharmacists itself, so its stock went unsold.

More than 7,000 Dutch patients depend on Bedrocan products, according to DVHN. The bankruptcy covers only the Dutch companies; Bedrocan's Danish and Canadian subsidiaries are outside the filing, Forbes reported. Dutch authorities have said existing stocks should cover patients in the Netherlands until at least mid-2027, and the state office plans to move to imported cannabis during 2027 through a European tender.

Italy has leaned on Dutch imports for years because domestic production is small. The only authorised grower is the military's chemical-pharmaceutical plant in Florence. Health ministry data for 2024 show Italian pharmacies received 1,695 kilograms of medical cannabis, of which only a little over 200 kilograms were grown in Italy, Il Post reported. By that count, close to 88% of supply came from abroad. The International Narcotics Control Board put Italy's need for 2025 at 2.4 tonnes, well above what pharmacies actually received in 2024.
Private companies are legally allowed to grow medical cannabis in Italy, but none do. A 2022 call selected six companies and nothing followed, MMJDaily reported.

Other producers can step in, but not overnight. At a press conference held by the Luca Coscioni Association, Meglio Legale and Forum Droghe, pharmacist Marco Ternelli said suppliers already serving Italy would need much larger import authorisations from the health ministry's central narcotics office, which are renewed annually and tend to follow past volumes, Farmacista33 reported. He also warned that replacement strains will not match the THC and CBD ratios patients are used to, so many will need a doctor's review and a new prescription. Bedrocan's Danish farm has less capacity, fewer varieties and existing demand from Germany.

In the UK the numbers are small but the stakes are high. About seven prescriptions for Bedrolite, a high-CBD, low-THC oil made by Glasgow-based Target Healthcare, are affected, mostly children with treatment-resistant epilepsy, according to the Medical Cannabis Clinicians Society. Bedrolite is grown only in the Netherlands and sits inside the bankruptcy estate. Bedrocan has said it would take at least six months to bring the variety into production in Denmark, and Target has told families it holds roughly six months of stock.

MPs heard on 15 October that one family's supply could run out in December. In a written answer on 19 October, health minister Baroness Merron said the British Embassy in The Hague is in contact with the Dutch health ministry about the impact on UK patients, while clinical decisions remain a matter for each patient's doctor. A Commons answer the same day said the same. The society has asked the government to seek an emergency release of existing stock, similar to the 2021 arrangement that kept Dutch supply flowing to NHS patients after Brexit.
> One ended contract in The Hague has reached pharmacy counters in Rome and children's bedrooms in Britain within weeks. Europe's medical cannabis supply has fewer backstops than its size suggests.

For EU-GMP producers already licensed to ship to Italy, the gap is an opening, but it opens only as fast as import permits allow. Italy's dependence on a single channel also strengthens the case its patient groups have made for domestic private cultivation. In the Netherlands, the 2027 import tender becomes the next big contract on the continent, and in Germany, where prices are already falling, as we reported on 8 November, any diversion of Danish supply toward Italy would tighten a market that has been running in buyers' favour.

Watch whether the trustee sells the stock, and with it the Bedrolite genetics, to a buyer the Dutch office approves; whether Italy's narcotics office raises import quotas for other suppliers; whether London and The Hague agree an emergency export route before UK stock runs low around the turn of the year; and the design and timing of the Dutch 2027 tender.
